title: Saronic Corsair sea drone picks up two Apache crew off Oman and carries them to a helicopter hoist
summary: A Navy Corsair sea drone picked up two Apache crew off Oman and carried them to a helicopter hoist; CENTCOM reported that both were rescued within about two hours.
account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.
purpose: The Corsair is an autonomous maritime platform that Task Force 59 had been fielding since late March 2026. In this case, the military used it to carry stranded crew members to a helicopter recovery point.
system: Saronic Corsair unmanned (autonomous) surface vessel operated by U.S. 5th Fleet's Task Force 59
deployer: U.S. Navy, 5th Fleet Task Force 59 (U.S. Naval Forces Central Command)
location: Off the coast of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz
domain: Military search and rescue / personnel recovery at sea
segment: Government, security, and defense (naval unmanned surface vessels)
taxonomy_note: An at-sea rescue of aircrew is read as a health outcome because no rescue type exists.

ratings.reason: Two aviators were recovered from the water and transferred to a helicopter within approximately two hours, according to CENTCOM. Their condition was stable. The sources do not establish the counterfactual risk of death or whether another rescue asset could have reached them.

The military recovered two crew members using an unmanned vessel and a helicopter. The sources describe a successful operational recovery but do not isolate the AI’s contribution or quantify an organizational saving.

ai_role.statement: Hawkins identified an unmanned Corsair as the recovery vessel. DefenseScoop describes the platform’s autonomous capabilities, but its suggestion that passive sensing helped locate the crew is an inference. The official sources do not identify the navigation mode, human supervision, or sensor contribution during this rescue. A crewed helicopter completed the recovery.

fields.account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.

fields.account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.

produced_by: A Corsair already deployed with Task Force 59, which began fielding these vessels in late March 2026
A vessel able to carry the crew to a location that a rescue helicopter could reach
A crewed helicopter and coordinated military rescue effort
